Description: Transaction-level synthetic target: 1 for a suspicious AML overlay and 0 for a legitimate baseline transaction.
Derivation rule: Set to 1 when a suspicious typology overlay generates the transaction; otherwise set to 0 for the legitimate baseline.

Description: Unique synthetic identifier for the transaction; it is not a real banking identifier.
Derivation rule: Assign a unique synthetic row identifier when transaction records are assembled.

Description: Synthetic transaction time of day, including salary or grant timing, routine spending periods, and rapid AML episodes.
Derivation rule: Sample from the account profile schedule, including salary or grant timing, ordinary spending windows, and typology-specific timing.

Description: Calendar date on which the synthetic transaction occurs within the observation window.
Derivation rule: Sample within the configured observation window after applying account activation and scenario scheduling rules.

Description: Synthetic identifier for the monitored receiver account used to group transaction histories.
Derivation rule: Generate a unique random 9 to 11 digit synthetic account number for each monitored account.

Description: Synthetic 9 to 11 digit account number on the sending side of the transaction.
Derivation rule: Select the sender endpoint from the monitored account or synthetic counterparty endpoint pool according to direction.

Description: Synthetic 9 to 11 digit account number on the receiving side of the transaction.
Derivation rule: Select the receiver endpoint from the monitored account or synthetic counterparty endpoint pool according to direction.

Description: Synthetic account number for the counterparty associated with the monitored transaction; repeated values support network analysis.
Derivation rule: Reuse or create a synthetic endpoint according to the customer's normal counterparties or the scenario network pattern.

Description: Transaction direction relative to the monitored account: Inflow or Outflow.
Derivation rule: Set relative to the monitored account from the selected sender and receiver endpoints.
Observed unique values: Inflow | Outflow

Description: Positive synthetic transaction value generated from customer profile, payment rail, timing, and behaviour distributions.
Derivation rule: Draw a positive amount from profile, payment-rail, timing, and scenario-specific distributions with realistic overlap between classes.
